o1.biggest_strength: It spots the real win: turn the paused 1-month pause back on for the no-time segment, stop blanket discounting, and make that the sprint critical path.
o1.biggest_mistake: The value model for the untested reminder and annual-plan saves is a little soft and would need clearer separation between proven saves and assumed saves before launch reporting.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the forecast into proven, assumed, and upside lines, and make the reminder action explicitly confirm that the learner is keeping the subscription.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a buildable one-screen flow with good segmentation, strong use of the pause, and mostly clear, friendly copy.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents customer-facing prices from ARPS and keeps a 50% discount for switchers without evidence, then partly counts that discount save too generously.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unsupported switching-app discount, use live billing variables instead of £9/£59.40 in copy, and make the revenue math distinguish discounted months from full-price retained months.

reason: Output 1 is the one I would rather hand to product: it puts the paused winner first, avoids wasting discounts, respects the cancel rule, and is more honest about the business risk. Output 2 is useful, but the unsupported half-price offer and invented prices make it less safe to ship.
